dataset.description:
The dataset will include quantitative, qualitative, and spatial data related to municipal resource management, demographic trends, and climate-related challenges in Latvian municipalities. Quantitative data will consist of statistical indicators on population dynamics, municipal budgets, land use, environmental indicators, and socio-economic development. Spatial data (GIS) will include territorial planning data, land use information, and climate-related spatial datasets. Qualitative data will include information collected through expert interviews, stakeholder consultations, workshops, and Living Lab activities conducted during the research.
The data will be obtained from several sources, including publicly available national databases such as the Central Statistical Bureau of Latvia, open government data portals, municipal development planning documents, and climate scenario datasets. Additional primary data will be collected during the research through interviews, surveys, and participatory workshops involving municipal representatives, experts, and other stakeholders.
The dataset will be used to analyse the relationships between demographic change, climate challenges, and municipal resource management. It will support the development and testing of an integrated methodology for smart governance of municipal resources under conditions of uncertainty. The data will also contribute to modelling, comparative analysis between municipalities, and the evaluation of governance solutions developed through the Living Lab approach.

distribution.title:
The purpose of the data collection and generation is to support the analysis of how municipalities manage resources under conditions of uncertainty, including demographic changes, climate-related risks, and socio-economic transformations. The collected data will enable the identification of key factors affecting sustainable municipal development and resource governance.
The data will be used to assess existing governance practices, evaluate the capacity of municipalities to respond to climate and demographic challenges, and analyse spatial and socio-economic development patterns. In addition, qualitative data generated through interviews, stakeholder consultations, and Living Lab activities will help understand decision-making processes, institutional barriers, and opportunities for improving participatory governance.
Overall, the data will serve as an empirical basis for developing and testing an integrated methodology for smart municipal resource governance, supporting evidence-based decision-making and sustainable planning at the local level.

dataset.title: Dataset on Smart Governance of Municipal Resources under Conditions of Uncertainty in Latvian Municipalities

dmp.description:
This doctoral research investigates smart governance approaches for municipal resource management under conditions of uncertainty, focusing on the impacts of demographic change, climate challenges, and spatial development dynamics on local governance. The study aims to develop and test an integrated methodological framework that supports municipalities in sustainable and data-driven decision-making. The research will apply a Living Lab approach, involving collaboration with municipalities and stakeholders to co-create and test governance solutions in real-life settings.
The research will use a combination of quantitative, qualitative, and spatial data. Quantitative data will include municipal statistical indicators, demographic and socio-economic datasets, climate scenario data, and financial information related to municipal resources. Qualitative data will consist of expert interviews, stakeholder consultations, workshop materials, and documentation generated through Living Lab activities. Spatial data will include GIS-based territorial data relevant to municipal planning and resource management.
Data will primarily be obtained from publicly available databases (e.g., national statistical data, open government data portals, and climate datasets), as well as primary data collected during the research, including interviews and participatory workshops. Interview and stakeholder data will be anonymized in accordance with ethical research standards and data protection regulations.
All research data will be securely stored on institutional storage systems provided by the university, with regular backups to ensure data integrity. Sensitive data will be stored in restricted-access folders and handled in compliance with GDPR and institutional data protection policies. Non-sensitive datasets and research outputs may be deposited in an open-access research data repository where appropriate.
Standard data management protocols will be followed, including clear documentation of datasets, metadata descriptions, version control, and secure storage procedures to ensure transparency, reproducibility, and long-term accessibility of research results.
dmp.ethical_issues_description:
The research may involve the collection of qualitative data through interviews, stakeholder consultations, and participatory activities with municipal representatives and other stakeholders. Therefore, ethical considerations related to personal data protection, confidentiality, and informed consent will be followed. All participants involved in interviews or workshops will be informed about the purpose of the research, the use of the collected data, and their rights as participants. Participation will be voluntary, and informed consent will be obtained prior to data collection.
Personal data will be anonymised or pseudonymised where necessary to ensure that individual participants cannot be identified in the research outputs. Sensitive information will not be publicly disclosed. Data handling and storage will comply with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requirements and relevant institutional ethical guidelines.
